post.summary: `POST /api/v1/bestellungen` — an online order (US1).
post.description:
The `Idempotency-Key` header is required once; the same key with the same
body answers with the first response, with another body `422
idempotency_key_reused`, and while the first is still being processed `409
idempotency_request_in_flight`.

Under `[policy] vertragsschluss = "mit_bestellung"` the Bestellnachweis,
the Bestellung, the contract, the Anmeldung's outbox command, the
documents' commands and the `de.mako.vertrag.bestellung.*` events commit in one
transaction (`201`). Under `"mit_annahme"` the order is stored
`EINGEGANGEN` and the contract waits for `…/annehmen` (`202`).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/events` — inbound CloudEvents from `makod` / `processd`.
post.description:
A confirmation moves the component into supply and, in the same
transaction, enqueues everything that follows from it: the GPKE
Beginnablesung, the tariff assignment `billingd` prices from, the billing
account, and — once every commodity is in supply — `de.mako.vertrag.aktiv`. None
of that is a detached task any more, so a restart mid-confirmation costs a
retry rather than a lost obligation.

get.description:
`404` until a Betreiber is recorded — billingd treats that as "no buyer
reachable" and its e-invoice findings say what is missing, exactly as an
unconfigured retail buyer does.

put.description:
The § 42b operator is a **Kunde**, not a Marktpartner: it has no MP-ID and
never appears in MaKo, but it is who the bundled GGV Sammelrechnung bills —
so the mapping from the operator-assigned `ggv_id` to a customer lives here,
beside every other buyer. Idempotent; a re-PUT moves the pointer.

get.description:
The `sub` comes from the **verified** token, then this answers whether that
customer owns `malo_id` within their site scope.

## Anti-enumeration

Every "not authorized" outcome — unknown sub, sub with no customer, customer
that does not own the MaLo, MaLo outside the identity's `standort_filter` —
returns the **same 403**. A distinct 404 for "no such customer" would let a
holder of any valid token probe which subjects and MaLo IDs exist
(DSGVO Art. 32). Only a genuine server fault returns 500.

422.description: A refusal naming the rule that decided

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/kunden/by-sub/{sub}` — resolve an OIDC subject to a customer.
get.description:
The response carries exactly the MaLos this identity may see, already
narrowed by its `standort_filter`.

## Whose subject is being resolved

A caller asking about **their own** subject is asking what the portal is
entitled to show them, so a customer token reaches it. Any other subject is
a foreign customer's profile, contracts and market locations, so resolving
one is an operator read. The two are different Cedar actions, chosen here by
comparing the path against the verified token — never by trusting the path.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/kunden/{id}/anonymize` — DSGVO Art. 17 right to erasure.
post.description:
Pseudonymises every personal datum — including the supply address — and
keeps the commercial record for § 147 Abs. 3 AO. Irreversible; the operator
is responsible for having identified the data subject first.

Answers **409** while contracts are still running: the data is needed to
perform them (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. b DSGVO), so Art. 17 Abs. 1 lit. a does not
apply yet. The response names the contracts, so the answer to the data
subject writes itself.

Art. 20 subset and the Art. 15 Abs. 1 lit. h statement `[policy.dsr]` decides.

put.summary: `PUT /api/v1/kunden/{id}/person` — store the BO4E `Person` of a B2C customer.
put.description:
The body is a `Bo4e<Person>`, so the gate — `_typ`, schema, strict enums,
BO4E rules — runs as `serde` deserialises it: `anrede` and `titel` are real
enum members, and the stored JSON is the canonical camelCase round-trip,
which is what makes a DSGVO Art. 15 disclosure structured rather than a
free-text blob. The strict-enum stage matters because the round-trip, not
the request, is stored, and a BO4E enum decoding to its `Unknown` catch-all
serialises back as the literal `"UNKNOWN"`, replacing what the caller sent.
A key BO4E does not define is refused ([`Bo4e::ensure_no_undefined_fields`](mako_markt::bo4e::Bo4e::ensure_no_undefined_fields)).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/kunden/{id}/rahmenvertraege` — create a framework contract.
post.description:
A Rahmenvertrag sets shared pricing, notice periods and billing terms for N
Versorgungsverträge below it — the model for portfolio customers with many
delivery points.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/kunden/{id}/vertraege` — create a supply contract.
post.description:
The contract, its components and the intent to register each commodity at
the NB commit together; the registrations are then performed by the outbound
worker, so neither a crash nor a `processd` outage loses one.

Idempotent on `erp_contract_id`: a replay returns `200` and dispatches
nothing.

## What is refused

- a term § 309 Nr. 9 BGB does not permit for a consumer, or an
  Ersatzversorgung running past the § 38 Abs. 4 EnWG three months;
- a gas component registered at the NB whose Anmeldung NN 44001 lacks a
  contract fact the column makes Muss — the Anlass, the Netznutzungsvertrag
  and its Zahler, the Gemeinderabatt, an Abrechnungsintervall, or the
  Kunde's name and address (UTILMD AHB Gas 1.2 Kap. 5.6). Each is named.

422.description: A refusal naming the rule that decided

put.description:
**Both bank identifiers are checked before storage**, so a typo is a 422 here
rather than a returned direct debit weeks later:

* the **IBAN** against ISO 7064 MOD-97-10, which catches every
  single-character error and every adjacent transposition;
* the **BIC** against the ISO 9362 grammar — 8 or 11 characters, letters
  where the standard requires letters. ISO 9362 defines no checksum, so this
  is a shape check and nothing more, but a mistyped BIC still routes a
  transfer nowhere and the shape catches most of them.

The body is a `Bo4e<Zahlungsinformation>`: the gate runs as it
deserialises, and a key BO4E does not define — `ibn` for `iban` — is refused
rather than stored under `_additional` beside an absent IBAN.

[`Bic`]: rubo4e::identifiers::Bic

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/malo/{malo_id}/produkte` — which product a MaLo is billed on.
get.description:
The single source of truth for the MaLo→product mapping. It is a contract
fact — agreeing it is a Tarifwechsel under § 41 Abs. 5 EnWG — so it lives
here, with the contract, and not in a catalogue that would have to be told
about it.

**Period form** (`?from=&to=`) is what `billingd` bills from: an invoice
covers a period, a Tarifwechsel inside it splits that period, and the answer
is the ordered slices tiling it. `[gueltig_von, gueltig_bis)` is half-open,
so consecutive slices share no day.

**Point form** (`?as_of=`, default today) answers the single-product
question.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Point form: the product in force on this day. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Period form (with `to`): every slice covering `[from, to]`.

get.description:
`billingd` selects the Modul 1/2/3 reductions it bills from this answer. A

get.description:
The Messstellenbetriebsvertrag the MSB holds at a Messlokation on `?on=`
(default today), plus the date a Kündigung received that day could take
effect.

`?on=` picks the contract as well as dating the answer: the same MSB may hold
successive contracts at one Messlokation, and the one that answers is the
latest to have begun by that day. An ended term still answers — `E_0200`
tells „bereits beendet" apart from „keine Zuordnung".

`processd` reads this to answer a WiM Kündigung MSB out of `E_0200`. A `404`
is **no contract** — the `ZC9` case; a `5xx` is a lookup that could not be
performed and must never be read as absence.

`?haushaltskunde=true` applies the § 309 Nr. 9 lit. c BGB one-month cap to
the contractual notice period.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description:
ISO 8601 date the contract is read as of and the next admissible
Kündigungstermin is computed against; defaults to today.

parameters.name: haushaltskunde
parameters.description:
Whether the Anschlussnutzer is a Haushaltskunde — decides the
§ 309 Nr. 9 lit. c BGB cap. Defaults to `true`, the protective reading.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/rahmenvertraege/{id}/kuendigen` — cascade termination.
post.description:
Terminates every live Versorgungsvertrag under the framework contract to the
same `lieferende`. Each child is checked against *its own* notice period —
the customer, the Vertragsart and the agreed period differ per site — so a
date that is lawful for most sites terminates those and reports the rest
rather than terminating none or terminating all unlawfully.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/vertraege/by-malo/{malo_id}` — the active contract behind a MaLo.
get.description:
The lookup `billingd` uses for the § 40 Abs. 1 EnWG contract facts an
invoice must state. Besides the contract row it computes the next possible
Kündigungstermin under the rules that actually apply to this contract, and
resolves the BG-7 buyer so the e-invoice has a real addressee.

# `?stichtag=YYYY-MM-DD`

The date the Kündigungsfrist is measured from; today when absent. `processd`
passes the **Eingangsdatum der Kündigung**, because that is what `E_0614`
Prüfschritt 70 names: „unter Einhaltung der Kündigungsfrist unter
Berücksichtigung des Eingangsdatums der Kündigung". Inside the one-Werktag
answer window the two usually agree; across a month boundary they do not,
and the answer would otherwise state a date a whole notice period out.

parameters.name: stichtag
parameters.description:
`?stichtag=YYYY-MM-DD` — the date a Kündigungsfrist is measured from.
Absent means today.

parameters.name: kunde
parameters.description:
`?kunde=<Name>` — the customer a market message names, for `E_0624`
Prüfschritt 50.

`processd` passes the `SG12 NAD+Z09` „Kunde des LF" of an inbound 55010
(or 44010). The answer comes back as `kunde_identisch_mit_anfrage`, and
it is deliberately tri-state — see [`domain::kundenidentitaet`].

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/vertraege/{id}/kuendigen` — terminate the contract.
post.description:
The notice period comes from the *reason*, not from the contract: an
ordinary termination runs on the agreed period (capped for consumers by
§ 309 Nr. 9 lit. c BGB), a Grundversorgungsvertrag on the two weeks of
§ 20 Abs. 1 StromGVV/GasGVV, a move on the six weeks of § 41b Abs. 5 EnWG,
and a price change ends the contract without notice on the day the change
takes effect (§ 41 Abs. 5 Satz 4 EnWG). A `lieferende` earlier than the rule
allows is refused with the rule quoted.

Everything then happens in one transaction: the components leave supply, the
Lieferende UTILMDs and the Schlussablesung are enqueued, and the
`de.mako.vertrag.kuendigung` CloudEvent — which carries the § 41 Abs. 8 Nr. 2
EnWG Textform confirmation the supplier owes the customer — goes into the
outbox.

422.description: A refusal naming the rule that decided

`GET /api/v1/vertraege/{id}/kuendigungsfrist` — the earliest end date per
reason.
get.description:
A portal that lets a customer terminate has to show the date *before* the
request, and an operator answering a letter has to quote the rule. Computing
it in the portal would put four statutes in a second place; asking here
keeps one answer.

parameters.name: eingang
parameters.description: When the notice arrives; defaults to today.

422.description: A refusal naming the rule that decided

put.description:
The body is a `Bo4e<Preisgarantie>`, so the gate runs as it deserialises —
for a `Preisgarantie` that includes the `Zeitraum` in `zeitlicheGueltigkeit`,
the very field `preisgarantie_bis` is derived from below and the one the
Tarifwechsel guard reads. A key BO4E does not define is refused
([`Bo4e::ensure_no_undefined_fields`](mako_markt::bo4e::Bo4e::ensure_no_undefined_fields)): a misspelt `zeitlicheGueltigkeit`
would otherwise store a guarantee with no end date.

Deriving `preisgarantie_bis` from the stored document means the Tarifwechsel
guard and the document the customer holds can never disagree.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/vertraege/{id}/stornieren` — cancel before supply began.
post.description:
Valid for `ANGELEGT` and `IN_BEARBEITUNG`. A registration still waiting in
the outbound queue is withdrawn with it; one already sent to `processd` has
to be cancelled there, and the response says which case this was.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/vertraege/{id}/tarifwechsel` — change a component's product.
post.description:
A Tarifwechsel changes price, not supply: no UTILMD is sent, and the MaKo
status is untouched.

## Two different acts

`initiator` is required, because the law treats them differently.
§ 41 Abs. 5 Satz 1 EnWG binds a supplier who exercises a reserved right to
change the contract, and Satz 4 gives the customer a fee-free termination
right *because* the supplier exercised it. A tariff the customer asked for
is an agreed change: it is confirmed, it carries no Sonderkündigungsrecht,
and it is not held to the supplier's notice periods.

## What is enforced for a supplier-initiated future change

- **§ 41 Abs. 5 Satz 3 EnWG.** `preise[]` states the Umfang of the change.
  Required where this deployment renders the Preisänderungsanzeige itself
  (`outputd_url` configured), because the lines are the document's content.
  Where the CloudEvent is the notice, the ERP composing the letter states
  the Umfang from its own price sheets, and the lines are optional — sent
  along when the caller has them, and marked absent on the event when not.
- **§ 41 Abs. 5 Satz 2 EnWG.** The customer is owed a month's notice (two
  weeks outside households); a Grundversorgungspreis needs the six weeks of
  § 5 Abs. 2 StromGVV/GasGVV. A Wirksamkeit too close to today is refused
  *here*, so the notice period cannot be missed by scheduling.
- **§ 5 Abs. 2 GVV.** A Grundversorgungspreis changes only at the start of a
  month.

## What is enforced for every Tarifwechsel

- **Preisgarantie.** A change taking effect inside the guarantee window is
  refused unless the operator overrides it, and every override is written to
  `preisgarantie_override_log` with the operator's token subject.

A retroactive correction (`wirksamkeit <= today`) is exempt from the notice
rules — it is not an announced price change but the repair of one already
agreed.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/vertraege/{id}/widerruf-kuendigung` — withdraw a Kündigung.
post.description:
Allowed while the Lieferende is still ahead. The queued Lieferende UTILMD
and Schlussablesung are parked in the same transaction; one that already
reached `processd` is the operator's to cancel there, and the response
names its component in `lieferende_bereits_versandt`.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/webhooks/angebot` — `de.mako.tarif.angebot.angenommen` from
`productd`.
post.description:
Creates the Rahmenvertrag and one Versorgungsvertrag per site, from the
**accepted variant of the BO4E `Angebot`**: what the customer was quoted and
what is contracted come from one document, so they cannot drift. The scalar
fields on the event are the fallback for a quotation accepted before it was
ever priced.

Idempotent twice over — on the CloudEvent id, recorded once the work is
done, and on `erp_rahmenvertrag_id = angebot_id` — so a redelivery creates
nothing, and a redelivery after a failure finishes the work.
